title: Trump Says US Will End $4 Billion in Yearly Military Aid to Israel; Congress Has a Say
dek: Trump said on Election Day that a deal with Netanyahu would end about $4 billion in annual US military aid while arms sales continue. Reporting differs on timing, and the change would need Congress.
author: Meridian Newsroom

image.alt: The U.S. Capitol, west front (file photo)

keyPoints: Trump said Tuesday that the US would stop providing about $4 billion a year in military aid to Israel, following a deal he said he reached with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, according to AP and NBC News.

AP reported that the US would keep selling arms to Israel. NBC and the New York Times reported that Trump said the aid would be cut off at the end of the year; AP reported the change as taking effect in 2027.
NPR reported that an abrupt end would be all but impossible, and that Congress will have a large say. The current memorandum of understanding does not expire until 2028.
Israeli opposition leaders Gadi Eisenkot and Yair Golan criticized the move, Golan saying it would deal a "severe blow to Israel's security" (AP).
body:
President Donald Trump said Tuesday that the United States will stop sending about $4 billion a year in military aid to Israel, saying the change was the result of an agreement with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. The announcement came on Election Day.

## What was announced

AP reported that Trump said the U.S. will stop providing $4 billion in aid each year to Israel in 2027, but will keep selling arms to Israel, which it called its closest Middle East ally. NBC News reported that Trump said he had made a deal with Netanyahu for the U.S. to stop sending the money annually. POLITICO described the announcement as unusually timed for Election Day and said it could set up a standoff with Congress.

The New York Times reported that Trump said the bulk of American aid to Israel would be "cut off at the end of the year," under an agreement reached with Netanyahu months ago. The Washington Post reported that the funding is for Israeli arms purchases.

The reports differ on timing, so this story does not give a single effective date.

## Congress and the agreement

NPR reported that the aid has been a major part of the U.S.-Israel relationship for decades, and that a 2016 agreement provided $38 billion over 10 years, or $3.8 billion a year. NPR also reported that the current memorandum of understanding is not set to expire until 2028, and that an abrupt end would be all but impossible without Congress. NPR said a more likely path is a wind-down of the current agreement if Congress agrees, and that it is unclear whether that could start as early as 2027.

## Reaction in Israel

AP reported that Eisenkot, a former military chief and Netanyahu's main rival, said Israel's defense establishment was learning of the shift "through the media." Golan, a former deputy military chief, said ending U.S. military aid would be a "severe blow to Israel's security" while Israel fights on multiple fronts.

## What is not yet known

Meridian has not confirmed a written order, a formal notice to Congress, or the exact amount of the final year of aid. Those details were not in the reporting reviewed for this story.
